newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end down on technical, foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end down on technical, foreign selling.

text.p: Technical and foreign fund selling pulled down blue-chip shares, reversing a fortnight-long rising trend, brokers and analysts said on Wednesday.
They said the fall in blue-chip prices also triggered selling and profit-taking in other shares.
The benchmark Composite Index shed 7.55 points to end at 1,119.28. The second board index eased 8.3 points to 554.62.

"The technical correction (argument) is only partly correct. There are still some foreigners waiting to unload their positions in Malaysia," said Phua Lee Kerk, head of research at Jupiter Securities.
He said rumours about Malaysia reporting a trade deficit in April also affected sentiment. Volumes were low, suggesting that the selling was not very widespread, he said.
Around 206 million shares were traded. Gainers trailed losers 97 to 488 and 152 stocks were unchanged.
Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at Capitalcorp, earlier said the market's rise from 1,070 on May 20 was "not followed by strong volume".
Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank Bhd, which is expected to release its annual results on Wednesday, bucked the general trend to end 30 cents higher at 16.40 ringgit.
The shares of Esprit Group was suspended just after lunch at the request of the company, a Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange official said. The share was unchanged at 11 ringgit.

Many dealers said the fall in share prices also showed that they were being propped up by some local funds. "Today, local funds were not in, so they have gone down," said a dealer with a bank-backed brokerage firm.

The dealers said most of the gains in the last few days were due to pushing up of select blue chips like Telekom Malaysia and Tenaga Nasional. Telekom was steady at 12.60 ringgit and Tenaga was down 10 cents at 11.90.

"It is also clear that the recent rise in the Composite Index was quite artificial. There were hardly any participants, just pushing up of select shares," said the head of research at another securities company.
